## An adventure itinerary through three countries: what is actually included

On a journey featuring [Argentina](/argentina/), [Bolivia](/bolivia/) and [Colombia](/colombia/), it is easy to imagine three equally active stages. The current Ada Tours programme offers very different forms of travel: developed walkways at Iguazu, Bolivia's high-altitude roads and a full sightseeing day near Medellín. **The main adventure is the two-day four-wheel-drive journey across Bolivia's Altiplano**, not a continuous trek on foot through all three countries.

This themed selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also includes Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Peru and Ecuador. Thus, the Argentina–Bolivia–Colombia combination page shows countries and a theme that coincide within an extensive journey; **it does not promise a ready-made tour covering only three countries**.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If you are interested in travel through these three countries beyond the adventure theme, see the [general Argentina + Bolivia + Colombia selection](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_colombia/). For this theme, the questions are different: which sections require physical preparation, where the borders are actually crossed and when there is time to rest.

## Argentina: walking routes at Iguazu

The Argentine section of the extensive tour begins after viewing the falls from the Brazilian side. Near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), the group follows walking routes on the Argentine side, including the [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/) area. A flight to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a city sightseeing tour and a tango show with dinner follow.

Iguazu offers a nature-park walk with striking views and the possibility of heat, humidity and rain. However, the published programme **does not advertise multi-day trekking, rafting or climbing in Argentina**. This is important when choosing: anyone seeking a sporting itinerary should check the activities actually included rather than rely solely on the interest label.

The Bird Park and Macuco Safari belong to the Brazilian section and are listed as optional services. They must not be presented as included adventures on the Argentine leg.

## Bolivia: 4×4 vehicles, lagoons and the salt flat

Travellers approach Bolivia via [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile, where the programme includes a stop before the high-altitude section. After the border crossing, the 4×4 journey begins. The first day links [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Dalí Desert, Polques thermal springs, Sol de Mañana geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The next day continues past high-altitude lagoons, Ollagüe volcano and the Chiguana Salt Flat to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

This is an overland expedition with stops at natural attractions. Its difficulty is determined not by the length of a walking trail but by altitude, bumpy roads, cold, early departures and the remoteness of individual sections. The tour description mentions stretches **above 4,000 metres** and the risk of altitude sickness. Fitness may make walking easier, but it does not eliminate altitude-related symptoms; discuss your health and an appropriate pace with a medical professional before buying flights.

| Bolivian section | Main characteristic |
|---|---|
| Laguna Verde | Altitude, wind, volcanic scenery |
| Polques and Sol de Mañana | Geothermal stops |
| Laguna Colorada | High-altitude lagoon, flamingos |
| Uyuni | Salt, open plain, photography stops |

The latter part includes visits to Colchani and the Incahuasi Island area. Conditions at Uyuni change with rainfall: a dry surface and a mirror effect after rain offer different experiences and can affect travel across the salt flat differently. As an alternative to this extensive itinerary, explore [adventure tours featuring Bolivia](/interests/adventure/tours/bolivia/), comparing especially the actual length of the high-altitude section.

## Colombia: Guatapé and an active excursion without a multi-day trek

The Colombian section begins only after the Peru and Ecuador parts are complete. A flight from Guayaquil takes travellers to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The following day features an eight-hour excursion to El Peñol and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/): reservoir views, the El Peñón rock monolith and walks through a town known for its painted building fronts.

It is important to distinguish **seeing the rock** from **climbing its steps**. The published tour description includes a visit to the monolith and a town tour, but it does not guarantee an ascent to the summit as a separate included service. If this is your reason for choosing Colombia, confirm whether the climb is necessary, whether the steps are accessible and what level of exertion is suitable while agreeing on the itinerary.

The journey continues to [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) in Medellín, [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) with Monserrate, followed by a trip to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). These are city and cultural excursions, not another block of rafting or mountain trekking. Anyone looking specifically for sporting activities in Colombia should also compare [adventure tours in Colombia](/interests/adventure/tours/colombia/) based on confirmed activities.

## Why the stages cannot be joined by a short “Argentina – Bolivia – Colombia” flight

The order of the existing journey is more complex: after Argentine Iguazu and Buenos Aires, the route visits Uruguay, then flies to Chile and crosses Bolivia's highlands. **Peru and Ecuador lie between Bolivia and Colombia**, with Machu Picchu and the Galápagos Islands along the way. Removing those countries would mean designing a different product with new connections, dates and terms.

Three questions are especially important for the adventure portions.

1. **Altitude and recovery.** Adaptation to altitude is needed before the two days in four-wheel-drive vehicles; more overland journeys and international flights follow. Travellers prone to altitude sickness should discuss a different pace before confirming the programme.
2. **Changing conditions.** Iguazu can be hot and humid, the Altiplano has cold winds and bright sun, and Cartagena has a tropical coast. One set of clothes is inconvenient for the entire trip.
3. **Borders and luggage.** The itinerary includes an overland Chile–Bolivia border crossing, then Bolivia–Peru, and several flights. Baggage limits for the specific flights, re-entry requirements and appropriate travel insurance should be checked.

We help break down the extended programme into flights, transfers and days of exertion, clarify documentation requirements by traveller nationality and agree on a gentler pace where actual bookings allow it. Calling a tour “adventurous” does not guarantee a trekking instructor, specialist equipment or additional sporting excursions.

## Who will enjoy this combination

Choose this combination for its **contrasts**: Argentina's waterfalls, an overland expedition through Bolivia, and Colombia's mountainous and urban landscapes. However, the journey is long and includes five further countries. Those who want to focus on Bolivia and reduce the number of flights may find it more useful to compare shorter itineraries in the [general adventure section](/interests/adventure/) and the actual content of [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia

### Is the climb up El Peñón in Guatapé included?

The published 32-day tour confirms a visit to the rock area and a sightseeing excursion in Guatapé. A climb to the summit is not listed as a separate included activity. Its availability and conditions should be agreed before travel.

### Do I need specialist hiking equipment for Bolivia?

The Altiplano four-wheel-drive route mainly involves driving and stops. Warm layers, protection from wind and sun and comfortable shoes are essential; any specialist equipment depends on specific additional activities and must not be assumed to be included.

### Do Iguazu and the Medellín excursions count as extreme sports?

No. On our tour, these are walks and sightseeing excursions. The main expedition-style demands come from Bolivia's high-altitude section.

### Can I visit just the three selected countries?

That would require a separately designed itinerary. The existing ready-made programme covers eight countries, and its flights, transfers and stops depend on the entire route.

## Three historical stories on one journey

[Argentina](/argentina/), [Bolivia](/bolivia/) and [Colombia](/colombia/) offer an unusual combination of cultural experiences. In Argentina, the programme explores neighbourhoods and tango. In Bolivia, the principal historical attraction is **Tiwanaku**, the centre of a civilisation that existed long before Inca rule in the Andes. In Colombia, travellers move from Medellín's street art and urban history to Cartagena's fortifications and Bogotá's museum collections.

The Ada Tours catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with these countries and a culture-and-history focus. The [32-day, eight-country South American itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also includes Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Peru and Ecuador. This is **one extensive journey**, not a published tour exclusively through Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia. The cultural stops described are separated by days spent in other countries.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If geography and total duration are your priorities, see the [Argentina + Bolivia + Colombia route selection](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_colombia/). Here, the focus is on what the three countries reveal about their past and present-day life.

## Argentina: Buenos Aires neighbourhoods and tango

The Argentine part of the 32-day programme begins with walks at Iguazu Falls before moving on to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The city tour includes [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/), San Telmo, Recoleta and Puerto Madero; an evening tango show with dinner is also scheduled.

These districts reveal different sides of the city. La Boca is known for colourful façades and its port history, San Telmo for old streets and city squares, and Recoleta for elegant architecture and its historic cemetery. Tango is a natural continuation of the Buenos Aires experience: its dance and music are bound up with the urban culture of the Río de la Plata region. This is a specific part of the itinerary, not an abstract suggestion to “try local art”.

For more in-depth exploration of individual neighbourhoods, compare [cultural programmes in Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/). The present 32-day journey allocates limited time to Buenos Aires because a major international leg comes next.

After the capital, there is a one-day ferry trip to Montevideo and back to Argentina. **Uruguay is a fourth country actually visited during this stage**, so documentation should not be planned solely around the three countries named in this selection.

## Bolivia: pre-Inca Tiwanaku and modern La Paz

The Bolivian section begins with a high-altitude four-wheel-drive journey towards Uyuni, but the most relevant stops for the Culture and History theme come later. After a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), a city tour is scheduled, followed by a journey to the [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) archaeological complex before crossing into Peru.

Tiwanaku was the centre of an independent pre-Columbian civilisation on the Andean plateau. Stone structures of its ceremonial complex survive, including **Kalasasaya and the Gate of the Sun**. The site is a UNESCO World Heritage property. It illustrates how Andean cultural history began long before the internationally famous Inca monuments of Peru.

Visiting Tiwanaku involves more than the guide's commentary. The archaeological complex stands at roughly 3,850 metres; by then the route has already traversed high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni and La Paz. When choosing the journey, consider how altitude may affect well-being and how much time remains for an unhurried visit after transfers.

In [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the programme includes a city tour and the Valley of the Moon. This introduces the modern metropolitan area and its natural surroundings; it does not replace Tiwanaku. If archaeology is your chief interest, compare [culture-and-history tours featuring Bolivia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/) by the time spent at archaeological sites.

## Colombia: from urban memory to colonial fortresses

The Colombian section starts in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The programme includes [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) and then continues via [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/).

In Medellín, the story behind the transformation of urban neighbourhoods matters as much as the murals. Comuna 13 provides an opportunity to discuss the city's recent history through public spaces and local artistic practices. The adjacent day includes a trip to El Peñol and Guatapé; that is a different kind of experience and should not be presented as a separate history museum.

Cartagena reveals another era. Its old town, city walls and fortifications reflect the history of Spanish colonial trade and defence of the Caribbean port. The sightseeing programme includes views of the bay, historic streets and San Felipe de Barajas Fortress. Cartagena's fortification ensemble is a UNESCO World Heritage property.

In Bogotá, the exploration of the past continues through the Gold Museum, the Botero collection, the historic centre and a visit to Monserrate. The itinerary then goes to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and the Salt Cathedral. This final stop adds another type of cultural attraction to the urban story: a religious space within former salt mine workings.

| Country | Cultural theme |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Tango and city neighbourhoods |
| Bolivia | Pre-Columbian Tiwanaku |
| Colombia | Fortresses, museums and urban memory |

These are distinct historical stories. Treating them all as one “Inca” or “colonial” theme would be inaccurate: the Tiwanaku civilisation, Buenos Aires' port culture and Cartagena's fortifications belong to different eras and regions.

## How to allocate days to historical attractions

Combining the three countries is complicated by the actual sequence of travel. After Argentina, the group visits Uruguay and Chile, then Bolivia. **Peru and Ecuador lie between Tiwanaku and Colombia**, with Lake Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Lima, Quito and the Galápagos Islands on the programme. Omitting these stops to create a shorter history tour would require redesigning flights and transfers.

For museum visits, check the days of the week and whether exhibitions are open. The published itinerary specifically notes possible closures of some Bogotá museums; opening hours must be confirmed for the intended date before a museum visit can be treated as guaranteed. At Tiwanaku, the more important questions are the duration of the visit and a manageable level of activity at altitude.

We help match excursions to flight schedules and agree on overland transfers and the sequence of cities. On a journey through eight countries, documents must be checked for each traveller's nationality and for re-entry, including the return to Argentina after a day trip to Uruguay. Specific prices, tickets and guiding arrangements are defined by the chosen tour's terms, not by the general culture-and-history label.

## Choose historical depth or an overview of South America?

For someone who wants to experience **several completely different cultural traditions** in one journey, the extensive itinerary combines tango, an ancient Andean civilisation and Colombia's colonial heritage. If your main goal is to spend extended time in Bogotá's museums or study Tiwanaku, a busy journey through eight countries leaves less time than a specialised programme within one country.

For independent comparisons, begin with the [Culture and History section](/interests/culture-and-history/), then compare the sightseeing days on [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) and [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/). The meaningful distinction is the depth of each visit, not simply the number of countries.

## Frequently asked questions about historical itineraries in Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia

### Is Tiwanaku included in the current programme?

Yes. The 32-day itinerary includes travel from La Paz via Tiwanaku to the Peruvian border. The time allocated to the visit and well-being at altitude should be considered before the Bolivian section begins.

### Can I visit Colombia's museums and Cartagena in one day?

No. On our programme, Cartagena and Bogotá are separate stages with a flight between them. Bogotá's museums and sightseeing at fortified Cartagena require different days.

### Are there cultural excursions in Argentina besides tango?

Yes. The programme includes a city tour of Buenos Aires and its historic districts, followed by a tango show with dinner. These are two separate elements of the city experience.

### Why does a three-country selection describe an eight-country journey?

Because the filter lists all active tours whose main route includes Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia and whose themes match this interest. At present, the qualifying programme also covers five other countries; read the complete itinerary before booking.

## Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia: contrasting landscapes within one journey

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [extensive tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia as only part of its programme. The route also passes through Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Peru and Ecuador. That is why it is useful to consider the entire sequence of natural and cultural stops when choosing the trip.

The three countries offer different experiences. **Argentina** brings close-up views of Iguazu Falls amid subtropical forest. **Bolivia** offers volcanic highlands, lagoons and Uyuni's vast salt plain. **Colombia** features the green mountains around Medellín, the granite El Peñón rock and the winding bays of the Guatapé reservoir. City days in Buenos Aires, Cartagena and Bogotá retain a cultural emphasis.

## Argentina: getting close to Iguazu's cascades on boardwalks

The Argentine nature day begins after visiting the Brazilian side of [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). You cross the border towards [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). On the Argentine side, walkways follow individual streams and lead to viewing areas near [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/). This offers a chance to approach the water after the broad panoramas on the Brazilian side.

UNESCO describes the neighbouring national parks of Argentina and Brazil as a single waterfall complex in the Atlantic Forest. Its significance includes both the powerful cascades and the protected humid-forest ecosystem. However, the Argentine part of the chosen tour does not include a separate multi-day wildlife-watching programme: the itinerary focuses on the falls themselves.

[Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) comes next, with a city tour and tango. This journey **does not include the Argentine section of Patagonia with its glaciers**. If that is essential to you, choose a different itinerary rather than rely on the “Nature” theme label.

## Bolivia: highlands from Laguna Verde to Uyuni

The Bolivian section begins after [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile. The programme features a 4×4 journey through [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), desert plateaus, thermal springs and geysers to [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Here nature looks entirely different: mineral colours in the water, high volcanic peaks and plains almost devoid of vegetation.

The next four-wheel-drive day explores a chain of lagoons, volcanic slopes and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The salt flat looks different in dry and wet periods. Mirror-like water is a seasonal possibility, not a guaranteed part of the excursion; surface conditions also determine access to some areas. A flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) follows.

Altitude is a major factor in its own right. After lowland cities and humid Iguazu, travellers reach high-altitude areas relatively quickly. Discuss acclimatisation, overnight stays, cold, wind, hydration and insurance conditions before departure.

## Colombia: El Peñón rock and the green surroundings of Guatapé

In Colombia, the tour's clearest nature experience is the excursion from [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The rock rises over green scenery and a reservoir with numerous bays and islands. The programme includes the area itself and the town, known for the colourful relief decorations on its façades. Colombia's official tourism portal states that the reservoir was formed by a hydroelectric complex: its winding shoreline reflects both natural terrain and a man-made body of water.

The journey then turns to urban Colombia: Medellín, historic Cartagena, Bogotá and a trip up [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/) for city views. The underground Salt Cathedral in Zipaquirá is a cultural excursion within former mine workings; it should not be described as an independent exploration of a wild cave.

## The programme available to choose

| Tour | Duration | Main nature attractions |
|---|---|---|
| [Eight countries of South America](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | 32 days | Iguazu, Uyuni, Guatapé, Galápagos |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The complete programme also visits the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) in Ecuador, with separate excursions. They are **outside Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia**, but help explain why this extensive tour is so rich in nature experiences. For a different country combination, explore [nature in Argentina, Bolivia and Ecuador](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_ecuador/interests/nature/).

## Seasonality and practical preparation

Warm, humid conditions at Iguazu, dry high-altitude weather in Bolivia and the milder mountain climate around Medellín require different clothing. Pack a warm wind-resistant jacket and sun protection for the plateau, and clothes suitable for spray and rain at the falls. Travel at Uyuni and access to individual Iguazu viewpoints depend on natural conditions.

We can help coordinate nature days with domestic flights and the eight-country itinerary. It is especially important to assess altitude tolerance in advance and discuss any medical contraindications with a doctor. Documents must be checked for every country actually visited, including those not named in this selection's title.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia

### Does the selected tour visit both sides of Iguazu Falls?

Yes. According to the programme, travellers visit the Brazilian and Argentine sides on different days.

### Is a multi-day jungle trek included in Colombia?

No. The confirmed nature excursion visits El Peñón rock and the Guatapé reservoir; the other Colombian stops are mainly urban.

### Can I visit the Galápagos on this journey?

Yes. The full 32-day itinerary includes Ecuador and the Galápagos Islands. They belong to a different country and are not a Colombian attraction.

## Nature sections in three countries and wildlife watching in the Galápagos

Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia rarely fit into a short journey: they are far apart, and their most interesting natural areas lie in different climate zones. On our current tour, they form parts of a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Stops include Iguazu Falls, Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni, followed by Colombian cities and natural panoramas.

**The emphasis on nature is uneven across the countries.** In Argentina, it means humid forest and waterfalls; in Bolivia, high-altitude lakes and a salt plain; in Colombia, predominantly mountain scenery alongside city excursions. The programme includes no dedicated wildlife watching in Colombia. This is worth knowing in advance so that the interest label does not create an expectation of a safari in every country.

Between the three selected countries, the route also passes through Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Peru and Ecuador. Our selection covers programmes in which Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia are among the main countries, while the included wildlife-watching excursions take place during the Ecuadorian part of the complete tour. Other geographic options are available in the [general Argentina – Bolivia – Colombia selection](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_colombia/).

## Argentina: Iguazu Falls and humid tropical forest

An important nature stop on the Argentine leg is [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and the national park surrounding the falls. Its trails bring visitors close to different cascades and reveal the forest from a different side than the panoramic walk along the Brazilian bank. A group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide is included, after which the route continues with a flight to Buenos Aires.

The Atlantic Forest around the falls is exceptionally biodiverse. UNESCO notes a variety of birds, mammals and other wildlife here, including rare large predators. But **the presence of a species in a national park does not guarantee an encounter on a visitor trail**. The ordinary day at Iguazu is primarily for seeing the waterfalls and forest landscape, not spending hours searching for jaguars or tapirs.

Consider rainfall, water levels, path conditions and access to viewpoints when choosing a date. Some routes inside the national park may close temporarily. Non-slip shoes and protection for camera equipment against spray are useful. If particular wildlife encounters matter to you, they should be arranged separately from the main group excursion.

This extensive tour also includes the Brazilian side of Iguazu. It broadens the experience of the falls, but the two sides cannot be treated as visits to a single country: the Argentine park has its own facilities and entry rules. For other nature-focused itineraries, see [nature tours in Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/).

## Bolivia: flamingo lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat

Bolivia's nature section is very different from Iguazu. After travelling from Chilean Atacama, a high-altitude 4×4 route begins. The programme includes Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, Polques thermal springs, the Sol de Mañana geyser field and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Reddish water, mineral-rich shores, sparse vegetation and mountain peaks create the Altiplano landscape.

**Laguna Colorada is known for its flamingos**, but their behaviour and location vary. Observe the birds from a distance; their numbers, proximity to shore and photographic conditions depend on the season and weather. In the published tour, this section forms part of a general four-wheel-drive journey among lagoons; a specialised birdwatching expedition is not advertised as a separate service.

The following day continues through the Honda, Chiar Khota, Hedionda and Cañapa lagoons, Ollagüe volcano and the Chiguana Salt Flat towards [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The programme includes Colchani, sections of the salt plain and Incahuasi Island with its giant cacti. Uyuni is especially interesting in contrast with the previous day: colourful lagoons give way to an immense, flat expanse of salt. A mirror effect appears when weather conditions and surface water allow it; it cannot be guaranteed for any date.

**Altitude matters here.** Part of the journey runs above 4,000 metres. Long transfers, cold, dry air and the possibility of altitude sickness require preparation, particularly after the lower-lying parts of Argentina. Travellers who struggle with altitude should discuss the itinerary and medical restrictions with a doctor in advance. Water, warm layers, sun protection and suitable footwear matter even on a vehicle excursion.

[Nature tours in Bolivia](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/) offer other options to compare, but check not only whether Uyuni appears in the title but also the specific lagoons visited and the number of days spent at altitude.

## Colombia: mountain views without a promised safari

The Colombian part of this itinerary begins in Medellín. The programme includes an excursion to El Peñón rock and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), where the reservoir, green slopes and panoramas from above are the main nature experiences. Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá follow, with days focused mainly on cities, history and architecture.

This route is suitable for seeing Colombian landscapes alongside a cultural programme. **No dedicated trips to observe birds, mammals or tropical-forest wildlife in Colombia appear in the published itinerary.** It would be inaccurate to classify the entire Colombian section as specialised wildlife tourism simply because the full journey carries a nature-related tag.

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the programme includes a city tour and a trip up Monserrate. Views of the mountains and valley convey the altitude of the Andes, but the experience is different from a tropical national park at Iguazu or Bolivia's remote lagoons. Cartagena adds a coastal city; however, beach holidays and marine wildlife watching are not mandatory components of the Colombian section described here.

If Colombia's wildlife is your main goal, you can discuss a customised itinerary that adds specialist areas and extra days. The [wildlife-watching tour selection](/interests/wildlife/) covers more destinations, while [nature tours in Colombia](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/) should be assessed by their individual days and actual excursions.

## Important: the Galápagos Islands are in Ecuador

On the same 32-day tour, an included Galápagos sea excursion follows one of two routes: North Seymour and Bachas or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. The programme describes encounters with birds, sea lions and other island wildlife; the chosen route is confirmed after booking. This is the basis for the full journey's Wildlife Watching theme, but **the Galápagos Islands are in Ecuador, not Colombia, Bolivia or Argentina**. Galápagos birds and marine animals must not be attributed to the Colombian section simply because they feature on the same tour.

For travellers choosing a journey specifically for its wildlife, this geography matters: the richest wildlife-watching days may take place in another country on the same long route. Read the full itinerary rather than relying only on three selected countries in a filter.

## Comparing the three nature sections

| Country | Nature section |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Iguazu Falls and humid forest |
| Bolivia | High-altitude lagoons and Uyuni |
| Colombia | Guatapé, El Peñón and Andean panoramas |

Flamingos may be encountered at the Bolivian lagoons. Separate wildlife-watching excursions are not specified in these three sections; the included Galápagos programme takes place in Ecuador.

In the first country, walkways and water matter; in the second, altitude, temperature and long off-road journeys; in the third, mountain views combined with cultural stops. The time spent in each area follows the confirmed itinerary, not the fact that all three countries appear in the selection.

Over 32 days, altitude, climate and transport continually change. Bring protection from rain and humidity for Iguazu, warm clothing and sun protection for Bolivia, together with care when acclimatising, and comfortable shoes for Colombian city excursions. Check all entry and transit documents for the eight countries on the route according to each traveller's nationality. Domestic flight rules and included services should also be checked separately.

Ada Tours helps align nature days with realistic expectations. If photographing wildlife is your main goal, it makes sense to allocate more time to specialist excursions and clarify guiding arrangements rather than rely on chance encounters during ordinary sightseeing.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Bolivia and Colombia

### Does one tour include Iguazu, Uyuni and Colombia?

Yes. The [32-day, eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes the Argentine side of Iguazu, Bolivia's lagoons and Uyuni, followed by Medellín, Guatapé and other Colombian cities. Other countries are visited between those sections.

### Can I be guaranteed to see flamingos at Laguna Colorada?

No. The lagoon is known as flamingo habitat, but the presence of birds at a particular spot and viewing conditions depend on nature. The programme promises a route among lagoons, not a guaranteed wildlife photo session.

### Is the Bolivian section suitable if I do not tolerate altitude well?

Part of the route runs above 4,000 metres. Assess your tolerance of altitude in advance, discuss your health with a doctor and agree on potential itinerary changes before booking.

### Is there a separate wildlife-watching excursion in Colombia?

The 32-day tour examined includes no such independent excursion. The Colombian days focus on cities, Guatapé and other sightseeing. A dedicated wildlife programme would have to be arranged separately.

### Are the Galápagos included in the Colombian section?

No. They are visited during the Ecuadorian section of the same extensive journey. They must not be confused with Colombia's natural attractions.

## What links Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador and Colombia

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. At present, this is the [“8 South American countries in 32 days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It genuinely visits all four countries in the selection, but also travels through Brazil, Uruguay, Chile and Peru. These intermediate stops matter: from Argentina, travellers fly to Chile, continue overland into Bolivia, complete the Peruvian section and only then arrive in Ecuador. The flight to Colombia follows the Galápagos Islands.

It is therefore better to assess this journey as a sequence of very different regions rather than four neighbouring countries on a map. Cultural days in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and Colombian cities alternate with remote highlands and island nature excursions.

## Argentina: tango and an urban introduction before the Andes

The Argentine section includes both sides of Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires. In the capital, a sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide and a tango show with dinner are planned. This is a substantial cultural stage: La Boca, San Telmo, Recoleta and the city centre feel very different from other stops on the extended itinerary.

Travellers do not then head directly to Bolivia: the programme first includes a flight to Santiago, Chile, and a journey via Calama to San Pedro de Atacama. Consider this connection when comparing duration and cost with [Argentina-only tours](/argentina/tour/). A separate itinerary covering only the four named countries would require a different network of flights.

## Bolivia: four-wheel-drive vehicles, the salt flat and altitude-sickness risk

The route enters Bolivia across the high-altitude border with Chile. A two-day journey in 4×4 vehicles with an English-speaking guide includes Laguna Verde, geothermal springs, Laguna Colorada, other lagoons and salt flats. It is followed by [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and a journey towards Tiwanaku.

Unlike a city sightseeing tour, this section requires preparation for elevations above 4,000 metres, cool nights and travel on unpaved roads. The programme includes a stop in San Pedro de Atacama to aid acclimatisation, but each person's tolerance of altitude is different. Travellers with cardiovascular or lung conditions should consult a doctor before the trip. A considered pace and the ability to respond to symptoms are more useful at altitude than relying on fitness alone.

From Bolivia, the tour continues through Peru, via Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu. There is no direct La Paz–Quito leg in this itinerary: removing Peru would change both the logistics and the experiences.

## Ecuador: from Quito to the Galápagos

The Ecuadorian section starts in Quito, with a city tour and a visit to the equator-line area. A flight to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) follows, with a stay on Santa Cruz and a sea excursion. The shift from an Andean capital to islands with a different climate is particularly striking after weeks in the highlands.

The island section offers **two possible itineraries, only one of which is undertaken**: North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. Both must not automatically be promised as included. A TCT transit-control card is mandatory for the Galápagos; the process of obtaining it, flight documents and accommodation arrangements must be checked before departure from mainland Ecuador.

The nature experience here differs from Bolivia's. The high-altitude lagoons are notable for their landscapes, while the Galápagos sea excursion focuses on observing an island ecosystem under protected-area regulations. If wildlife is your main reason for travelling, explore [tours under the Wildlife and Safari interest](/interests/wildlife/) and the specific island programme included in your chosen tour.

## Colombia: from Medellín and Cartagena to Bogotá

After the Galápagos, the programme includes a flight via Guayaquil to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The itinerary features [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñón rock, followed by Comuna 13 and a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The final part visits [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and the Salt Cathedral in [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

These are three different urban experiences. Medellín and Guatapé offer green hills, panoramic viewpoints and an introduction to urban transformation; Cartagena is linked to the Caribbean coast and historic neighbourhoods; Bogotá stands in the Andes, where temperatures and physical exertion feel different again from the coast. Accommodation in Colombia should not be chosen solely on the basis of Cartagena's weather if the journey ends in Bogotá.

For this four-country selection, the Ecuador–Colombia connection is particularly significant. On our route, it is **a flight from Guayaquil to Medellín**, not an overland border crossing. The island flight from the Galápagos and the subsequent international connection call for careful checks of transfer times, baggage allowances and a contingency plan for delays.

## Documents, currencies and what the programme includes

For short tourist visits, Russian citizens appear on Colombia's official list of nationalities exempt from visa requirements. This applies only to permitted purposes of short-term entry; the immigration service makes the final decision. Requirements may differ for citizens of other countries or other types of visit. Conditions for Argentina, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador must be checked separately for the specific passport, transit arrangements and travel dates.

Argentina uses the peso, Bolivia the boliviano, Ecuador the US dollar, and Colombia the Colombian peso. The complete journey also involves currencies from the four additional countries. It is especially important to plan payment methods on the islands and during lengthy transfers; a Russian-issued or foreign-issued bank card from a particular bank is not guaranteed to work everywhere.

The [eight-country programme](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes domestic flights, 4-star hotels, transfers and the specified guided excursions. ## Frequently asked questions about Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador and Colombia

### Can I travel straight from Bolivia to Ecuador?

Not on the published 32-day itinerary: Peru lies between them, with Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima. A new itinerary with a direct connection would require a separate check of flights.

### Will the Galápagos include two excursion days to different islands?

The programme offers one of two island excursions. The specific option is confirmed when booking.

### How do travellers get from Ecuador to Colombia?

After returning from the Galápagos to the mainland, travellers fly from Guayaquil to Medellín. This section must not be treated as a road transfer across the border.

### Is the difficulty level the same on every stage?

No. City sightseeing and high-altitude four-wheel-drive travel have different demands. The most pronounced altitude risks arise in Bolivia, while sea conditions and protected-area access rules are more important in the Galápagos.
